name: Council Bluff
note: The reach the Corps reached on 30 July 1804, where the council with the Otoe and Missouria was held on 3 August. See docs/adr/0014-showcase-region-first.md: a Region is a heightmap plus this file.

points.name: council_bluff
points.note: The level bluff top closest to the river below it.

points.name: bluff_approach
points.note: The way up: higher ground behind the bluff, reached across the upland.

points.name: start
points.note: The landing, on the bottomland south of the bluff.

points.name: camp
points.note: Pitched a little back from the landing, along the bank.

points.name: landing_edge
points.note: Where the men step off toward the boats; the grass between is worn.

points.name: smoke_ridge
points.note: The highest hill in the western uplands.

points.name: mooring_0
points.note: The keelboat, loaded, needs the most water under her.

points.name: oto_meeting
points.note: Where the Oto and Missouria come in on 2 August: the open bottom beside the camp, where the Corps can walk out to them.

points.name: oto_approach
points.note: Where they come in sight: up the bottom from the south, in plain view of the camp. West of the camp the loess bench stands thirteen metres over the bottom, so nobody walks in from that side.

points.name: council_awning
points.note: Where the council sat on 3 August 1804: under an awning of the keelboat's mainsail, at the camp on the bottom, not up on the bluff.

landmark.name: Council Bluff
landmark.journal: Council Bluff — a high bluff above the river where the Corps will hold its first council with the Otoe and Missouria.

council.note: The sail awning the council met under. The council itself is the Scenario data/scenarios/council_bluff_1804.json.

village_smokes.note: The Oto and Missouria towns lie back off the river to the west, too far to walk to in the Slice. The ridge west of the bluff hides the feet of the columns, which is how Clark had the towns on his map days before the Corps saw one.

foliage.note: Loess bluffs over the Missouri bottom in August: cottonwood groves on the river, bur oak in the ravines, the upland prairie cured to straw. Tries are random points thrown at the map; each stand's own rules in foliage.gd decide which of them take.

groves.note: Bur oak country in the draws; the odd lightning-struck snag.

rocks.note: Loess country has few stones: an occasional weathered boulder, mostly in the draws.

foliage.wildflowers_note: The flowers of this reach in high summer, in stands of one kind: sunflowers in the bottoms, purple coneflower and blazing star on the dry upland, goldenrod coming on in the draws, yarrow underfoot everywhere. Lewis pressed all of them that season. 'low' keeps a species to the bottomland; false keeps it to the upland. Each kind needs a look in foliage.gd PROFILES.

wildlife.note: Game seen at a distance around Council Bluff, early August 1804. Clark noted elk and deer here; bison were not seen until 23 August, further upriver. A great egret was shot here on 2 August; the pelican raft is the flock Lewis measured on 8 August a little above. Cliff swallows nest in the loess under the bluff; vultures ride the thermal off its face.

_prairie_dogs: The dog town was moved out: the Corps first met prairie dogs on 7 September 1804, far upriver (docs/research/species-of-the-expedition.md). It belongs to that Region.
